slides.headline: 22% of my job titles were *never scored*
slides.subhead: Not scored low. Never classified at all. A rep works the list top down and cannot tell the two apart, because in the CRM they look exactly the same.

slides.headline: My scorer is a *ladder*, and a ladder has a floor
slides.body: It checks each rung in order. Anything that matches nothing falls through to other and scores low, silently, with no signal that it was never read.

slides.headline: *2,976* of 13,403 job titles
slides.body: could not be read by the ladder at all. Companies came out worse: 4,672 rows, which is 34.9%.

slides.headline: A low score and an unread row look *identical*

left.title: What the rep sees
items: A low score near the bottom

slides.quote: The fix is not a smarter model first. It is finding out how much of your own list your scorer cannot read.
slides.subhead: A better model on an unmeasured list just moves the guessing somewhere you cannot see it.

slides.headline: Go compute your own unclassified rate
slides.body: One number, on your own list, this week. It is the cheapest audit in your pipeline and almost nobody has run it.

verdict.lose: Trusting a score you never audited

slides.source: First party: 5 scored outbound lists, 13,403 rows, measured 2026-09-21
